claims.quote: Embedded within the cartilage matrix are chondrocytes, or cartilage cells, and the space they occupy are called lacunae (singular = lacuna).

claims.value: Chondrocytes are the cells that produce cartilage's matrix and its fibers.
claims.quote: The cells, called chondrocytes, make the matrix and fibers of the tissue.

source.citation: Clark MA, Douglas M, Choi J (2018). Biology 2e. OpenStax.

claims.value: A chondroblast becomes a chondrocyte once the matrix that chondroblasts produce (hyaluronic acid, chondroitin sulfate, collagen fibers and water) surrounds and isolates it.
claims.quote: This framework is a flexible, semi-solid matrix produced by chondroblasts and consists of hyaluronic acid, chondroitin sulfate, collagen fibers, and water. As the matrix surrounds and isolates chondroblasts, they are called chondrocytes.

source.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

claims.value: Cartilage has no blood vessels, so every nutrient must diffuse through the matrix to reach the chondrocytes, which is one reason cartilage heals very slowly.
claims.quote: Cartilaginous tissue is avascular, thus all nutrients need to diffuse through the matrix to reach the chondrocytes. This is a factor contributing to the very slow healing of cartilaginous tissues.

source.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

claims.value: The chondrocyte secretes a specialized, avascular, GAG-rich matrix and still keeps the ability to divide while embedded in cartilage matrix.
claims.quote: A skeletogenic cell that secretes a specialized, avascular, GAG-rich matrix, is embedded in cartilage tissue matrix, retains the ability to divide, and develops from a chondroblast cell.

claims.value: In the growth plate's proliferative zone, stacked chondrocytes divide by mitosis to replace the ones that die at the diaphyseal end of the plate.
claims.quote: The proliferative zone is the next layer toward the diaphysis and contains stacks of slightly larger chondrocytes. It makes new chondrocytes (via mitosis) to replace those that die at the diaphyseal end of the plate.

source.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

claims.value: Small chondrocytes in the growth plate's reserve zone take no part in bone growth; instead they anchor the plate to the bone of the epiphysis.
claims.quote: The reserve zone is the region closest to the epiphyseal end of the plate and contains small chondrocytes within the matrix. These chondrocytes do not participate in bone growth but secure the epiphyseal plate to the osseous tissue of the epiphysis.

source.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

claims.value: Long bones lengthen because chondrocytes divide and secrete hyaline cartilage.
claims.quote: Long bones lengthen as chondrocytes divide and secrete hyaline cartilage.

source.citation: Clark MA, Douglas M, Choi J (2018). Biology 2e. OpenStax.

claims.value: In a developing bone's cartilage model, the central chondrocytes enlarge; once their matrix calcifies, nutrients can no longer reach them, so they die and the cartilage around them breaks down.
claims.quote: As more matrix is produced, the chondrocytes in the center of the cartilaginous model grow in size. As the matrix calcifies, nutrients can no longer reach the chondrocytes. This results in their death and the disintegration of the surrounding cartilage.

source.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

claims.value: After a fracture, chondrocytes from the endosteum secrete a fibrocartilage matrix between the broken ends, forming an internal callus within about 48 hours.
claims.quote: Within about 48 hours after the fracture, chondrocytes from the endosteum create an internal callus (plural = calli) by secreting a fibrocartilaginous matrix between the two ends of the broken bone

source.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

claims.value: Growth hormone from the pituitary makes the chondrocytes in the epiphyseal plates multiply, which lengthens long bones.
claims.quote: The pituitary gland secretes growth hormone (GH), which, as its name implies, controls bone growth in several ways. It triggers chondrocyte proliferation in epiphyseal plates, resulting in the increasing length of long bones.

tier2.text: A chondrocyte is a cartilage cell that makes the matrix and fibers of cartilage; the matrix is the material around the cells. Each chondrocyte sits in a small space in the matrix called a lacuna. Cartilage has no blood vessels, so all nutrients must spread through the matrix to reach the chondrocytes. In the developing skeleton, chondroblasts produce cartilage matrix, and once this matrix surrounds and isolates a chondroblast, the cell is called a chondrocyte. In the limb bones and some skull bones, chondrocytes first make a cartilage model of the future bone; bone tissue then slowly replaces this cartilage over many years. A chondrocyte keeps the ability to divide even while embedded in the cartilage matrix. Growth hormone makes chondrocytes multiply in the epiphyseal plates, or growth plates, which are sheets of cartilage in growing bones; as a result, long bones get longer. Bones stop growing in length, however, when the chondrocytes in the epiphyseal plate stop dividing and bone replaces the cartilage.
